neighbours.label: The token that opens the next action in a past-tense story (the 'and' or subject before a new action verb: saw the hole and went; I said; He emptied), vs descriptive or opinion sentences
fire: The fox found the gate open and crept into the henhouse.
My brother called late that night. I answered and listened quietly.
The old woman heard a knock and hurried to the door.
By noon the well had run dry. He grabbed a bucket and walked to the river.
The farmer spotted the crow and threw a stone at it.
She asked whether I was free on Friday. I agreed and booked the tickets.
The boy reached the bridge and peered down at the water.
At dawn the camp was silent. She packed her bag and left.
quiet: Foxes are clever animals and often live near farms.
In my view, I believe that brothers should stay close.
The old woman is kind and lives near the church.
Wells are important sources of water in dry regions.
A farmer usually owns land and keeps several animals.
In general, I prefer Fridays because the office is quiet.
The bridge is made of stone and is very old.
Camps are usually quiet places with tents and fires.

predictions: The 'and'/subject opening the next narrated action reaches 0.2-0.6; descriptive or expository sentences with the same words stay under 0.08.
notes: Card: ' I' x7, ' You', ' and', ' He', ' peasant' in folk-tale or anecdote narration, each at the start of a new action. Probe: 'saw the hole and went' 0.604, 'I said yes' 0.272, 'He emptied the box' 0.214, 'The peasant opened' 0.191; 'I think that schools' 0.006, 'peasant class made up' 0.007, 'He is a tall man' 0.067.
